synth.title: Join It Up
synth.q: Join the two sentences into one. Use “too”.
synth.explain: too + adjective + for someone + to + verb. Don't add 'it' at the end: 'too heavy for Ravi to lift'.
synth.say: The box was very heavy. Ravi could not lift it.
synth.full: The box was too heavy for Ravi to lift.

synth.title: Join It Up
synth.q: Join the two sentences into one. Use “that”.
answers: that i could not drink it
synth.answer: that i could not drink it
synth.explain: so + adjective + that + result. With 'so … that' you DO need 'it'.
synth.say: The soup was very hot. I could not drink it.
synth.full: The soup was so hot that I could not drink it.

synth.title: Join It Up
synth.q: Join the two sentences into one. Use “enough”.
synth.s2: He can reach the top shelf.
synth.say: Ahmad is tall. He can reach the top shelf.
synth.full: Ahmad is tall enough to reach the top shelf.

synth.title: Join It Up
synth.q: Join the two sentences into one.
synth.explain: 'Unless' means 'if … not'. Unless you hurry = if you do not hurry. Don't write 'unless you don't'.
synth.say: You will be late. You must hurry.
synth.full: Unless you hurry, you will be late.

synth.title: Join It Up
synth.q: Join the two sentences into one. Use “nor”.
synth.explain: Neither … nor already means 'not'. Use a positive verb: 'came', not 'did not come'.
synth.say: Mrs Tan did not come. Mr Lee did not come.
synth.full: Neither Mrs Tan nor Mr Lee came.

synth.title: Join It Up
synth.q: Join the two sentences into one. Use “or”.
synth.s1: You can have the chicken rice.
answers: the chicken rice or the noodles
synth.answer: the chicken rice or the noodles
synth.explain: 'Either … or' gives a choice of two.
synth.say: You can have the chicken rice. You can have the noodles.
synth.full: You can have either the chicken rice or the noodles.

synth.title: Join It Up
synth.q: Join the two sentences into one. Use “but” … “also”.
synth.s2: He also sings in the choir.
answers: play the violin but he also sings in the choir
play the violin but also sings in the choir
play the violin but also sing in the choir
synth.answer: play the violin but he also sings in the choir
synth.explain: After 'Not only does …' the verb has no -s: 'play'. Then add 'but also'.
synth.say: Wei Jie plays the violin. He also sings in the choir.
synth.full: Not only does Wei Jie play the violin, but he also sings in the choir.

synth.title: Join It Up
synth.q: Join the two sentences into one.
synth.s2: The teacher could not hear the bell.
answers: that the teacher could not hear the bell
synth.answer: that the teacher could not hear the bell
synth.say: The children were noisy. The teacher could not hear the bell.
synth.full: The children were so noisy that the teacher could not hear the bell.

synth.title: Join It Up
synth.q: Rewrite the sentence starting with the words given.
synth.explain: Reported speech: 'I am' becomes 'she was'. The tense moves one step back.
synth.full: Lina said that she was hungry.

synth.title: Join It Up
synth.q: Join the two sentences into one. Use “whose”.
answers: whose cake was the prettiest won a prize
synth.answer: whose cake was the prettiest won a prize
synth.explain: 'Whose' shows that something belongs to a person: her cake → whose cake.
synth.say: The lady won a prize. Her cake was the prettiest.
synth.full: The lady whose cake was the prettiest won a prize.

synth.title: Join It Up
synth.q: Join the sentences starting with the words given.
answers: the rainy day we went for a picnic
the rain we went for a picnic
synth.answer: the rainy day we went for a picnic
synth.explain: 'In spite of' + a noun (the rainy day). No 'it was' after it.
synth.say: We went for a picnic. It was a rainy day.
synth.full: In spite of the rainy day, we went for a picnic.

synth.title: Join It Up
synth.q: Join the two sentences into one.
synth.explain: 'Before' + -ing: the person doing both actions must come straight after the comma.
synth.say: Kumar cleaned his room. He went to the playground.
synth.full: Before going to the playground, Kumar cleaned his room.

synth.title: Join It Up
synth.q: Join the two sentences into one. Use “and”.
synth.s1: We visited Grandpa on Chinese New Year.
synth.lead: We visited Grandpa on Chinese New Year
synth.explain: Use 'and' to add the second thing we did.
synth.say: We visited Grandpa on Chinese New Year. We brought him mandarin oranges.
synth.full: We visited Grandpa on Chinese New Year and brought him mandarin oranges.

synth.title: Join It Up
synth.q: Join the two sentences into one. Use “but”.
synth.s1: The void deck is quiet in the morning.
synth.s2: The void deck is busy in the evening.
synth.lead: The void deck is quiet in the morning
synth.explain: Use 'but' when the second part is different.
synth.say: The void deck is quiet in the morning. The void deck is busy in the evening.
synth.full: The void deck is quiet in the morning but busy in the evening.

synth.title: Join It Up
synth.q: Join the two sentences into one. Use “so”.
synth.s1: Mei Ling lives near the MRT station.
synth.s2: Mei Ling walks to the MRT station every day.
synth.lead: Mei Ling lives near the MRT station
answers: so she walks there every day
synth.answer: so she walks there every day
synth.explain: Use 'so' for the result of the first part.
synth.say: Mei Ling lives near the MRT station. Mei Ling walks to the MRT station every day.
synth.full: Mei Ling lives near the MRT station so she walks there every day.
